South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 78 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 04/14/26 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, and reassessment of fatigue and mood disorders.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit, primarily to assess his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) management, persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, and ongoing fatigue. He reports that despite adherence to his inhaler regimen, he continues to experience significant dyspnea, particularly during physical activity. He notes that he has been using the albuterol inhaler up to eight times daily, especially during periods of increased exertion, which he attributes to the recent fluctuations in weather.
The bilateral lower extremity edema remains a concern, with minimal improvement noted since the last visit. Mr. Fairfax continues to adhere to sodium restrictions and is compliant with furosemide therapy at the same dosage of 80 mg daily. The edema is still characterized as 1+ pitting, particularly exacerbated after prolonged periods of sitting, although he denies any associated pain, warmth, or erythema.
Mr. Fairfax expresses that his fatigue persists, significantly hindering his ability to engage in social activities and perform routine tasks. He also reports a worsening of his psychological symptoms, including increased anxiety and depressive episodes, which he feels are exacerbated by his chronic health conditions and limited mobility.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + daytime dyspnea, + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, increased use to eight times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 80 mg daily. 7. Sertraline 50 mg daily (ongoing management for anxiety and depression).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 82, BP 130/80, RR 26, O2 sat 87% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress but appears fatigued and anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.4, Hgb 11.3, Hct 34.0, Plt 205 2. BMP: Na 134, K 4.2, Cl 96, CO2 24, BUN 22, Cr 1.4, Glucose 92 3. BNP: 510 (slight increase). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.6 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: The patient continues to experience significant dyspnea despite ongoing therapy. Given the increased use of the albuterol inhaler, consider a reassessment of his inhaler technique and adherence. Reinforce the importance of pulmonary rehabilitation and assess for potential exacerbations. Follow-up in 1 month for reassessment. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema persists and has not improved. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and encourage Mr. Fairfax to elevate his legs. A nephrology referral will be arranged for further evaluation if no improvement is observed in the next follow-up. 4. Fatigue and psychological well-being: Given the ongoing symptoms of fatigue and exacerbated anxiety/depression, continue sertraline 50 mg daily. Schedule follow-up with a psychologist for ongoing support. Monitor CBC and metabolic panel in one month to assess for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
